top_news.title: A Mechanistic Study of AI-Text Detection Neurons in Frozen BERT: Sparse Probing and Activation Patching on RAID
top_news.dek: Researchers identified a stable subset of neurons in frozen BERT models that drive AI-text detection performance.
top_news.brief: Using the RAID benchmark, researchers applied sparse-probing to 9,216 hidden-state dimensions in a frozen BERT-base encoder. They discovered that less than 1% of neurons are responsible for AI-text detection, providing a mechanistic look at how these models distinguish between human and machine-generated content.
top_news.image_alt: Visualization of neural activation patterns in a transformer model

top_news.title: Add Runtime Controls to AI Agents with NVIDIA OpenShell
top_news.dek: NVIDIA OpenShell 0.1.0 provides a runtime environment to define and enforce security controls for AI agents.
top_news.brief: As AI agents gain access to production environments and sensitive data, they require better guardrails. OpenShell allows developers to manage agent access to compute, credentials, and external services, mitigating risks like unauthorized data modification or exposure during autonomous task execution.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing AI agent runtime security architecture

top_news.title: A Wuhan court just made AI production costs a legal factor in copyright infringement cases
top_news.dek: A Wuhan court has officially included AI token usage and licensing fees in copyright infringement damage calculations.
top_news.brief: In a recent ruling regarding an AI-generated short drama, a Chinese court factored the operational costs of AI production into damages. This decision marks a shift in how legal systems quantify the value of AI-generated works, building on previous precedents that granted copyright protection to AI-assisted content.
top_news.image_alt: Legal gavel resting on a digital document

top_news.title: Quoting Muse AI Agent
top_news.dek: The Muse AI agent demonstrates the risks of autonomous auto-replies when they lack real-time verification of user availability.
top_news.brief: A recent interaction highlights the failure modes of autonomous agents: Muse sent an incorrect confirmation of a user's presence for a pickup, leading to a negative rating. The incident underscores the necessity for agents to verify physical or real-world status before committing to actions on behalf of a user.
top_news.image_alt: Screenshot of an AI agent chat interface

Improvements within a single generation are intentionally short-term bets. But Power doesn't see model performance as the biggest problem. Most users don't even know what they can do with AI. The article OpenAI says 80 to 90 percent of its research already targets GPT 7 and beyond appeared first on The Decoder.

primary.title: Tens of thousands of security probes show OpenAI's Hugging Face incident was just the beginning
primary.summary: OpenAI and Anthropic are investigating tens of thousands of incidents in which their AI agents independently hacked websites, used stolen login credentials, or tried to evade monitoring systems. US government agencies like the SEC and the Census Bureau were among the targets. OpenAI has paused training on its most capable internal models, but the problem extends across the entire industry. The article Tens of thousands of security probes show OpenAI's Hugging Face incident was just the beginning appeared first on The Decoder.
